blocks.x: Switzerland is famous for its stunning autumn scenery–particularly its glowing golden larch forests and misty alpine valleys–but you don’t need an expensive overseas flight to experience it for yourself.

Nestled in the Pocono Mountains just two hours from New York City is Jim Thorpe, PA. But it’s not just your ordinary Pennsylvania mountain town–it’s America’s authentic answer to a Swiss alpine village, making it one of the absolute best fall day trips from NYC.

Home to tree-lined streets, dramatic cliffside views, and a vintage passenger train winding through the misty, mountain-ringed valley, this historic destination has rightfully earned its nickname, the “Little Switzerland of America.” Once its millions of trees become ablaze in shades of scarlet, copper, and gold, the town looks straight out of a movie set.

There’s a reason the Pocono Mountains were named the third best place to see fall colors in the U.S. by USA Today in 2022–the area’s 127 species of indigenous trees and shrubs put on quite the show for leaf peepers.

Beyond the stunning Jim Thorpe PA fall foliage, the destination is packed with Victorian mansions, charming streets filled with art galleries, boutiques, and artisan cafés, and the Lehigh Gorge Scenic Railway: a century-old passenger train takes you on a breathtaking 70-minute round-trip ride along the Lehigh River.
Here’s why adding Jim Thorpe, Pennsylvania to your fall bucket list before peak season is a must–and how to make the most of your visit.

Shutterstock / Desha Utsick
Jim Thorpe’s peak foliage is expected mid- to late October
Because the region spans 2,400 square miles of northeastern Pennsylvania, peak Pocono Mountains fall colors vary by zone, running from early through late October.

According to the official tourism boards, Jim Thorpe falls in the southern color zone. Currently, the trees are predominantly green, though Black Gum and Red Maple trees are beginning to display early red foliage, while Black Walnut is showing more widespread yellow.
The projected window for peak colors in Jim Thorpe is October 20–28, 2026.

Before locking in a visit date, check the latest Poconos Fall Foliage Forecast online or by calling 570-421-5565. It’s updated every Thursday through the end of October and will help you track exactly where and when the brilliant foliage is hitting its stride.

Getty / Ryan Kubishin
How to see Jim Thorpe at its most colorful
The best Jim Thorpe foliage day doesn’t require an overcomplicated schedule–strategic wandering is all you need!
Wander Jim Thorpe’s storybook streets

Start your day wandering Broadway and Race Street, the heart of Jim Thorpe’s historic downtown. The streets are lined with Victorian buildings, boutiques, and cozy cafés, while the town’s steep hillsides give it a distinctly alpine feel.
It’s the kind of place where you’ll keep stopping every few blocks because another postcard-worthy view has appeared.
For a glimpse at the town’s Gilded Age grandeur, tour the Asa Packer Mansion or check out the Harry Packer Mansion, a striking hilltop estate that reportedly helped inspire Disney’s Haunted Mansion.
Take a fall foliage ride through the Lehigh Gorge
Then, make the Lehigh Gorge Scenic Railway the centerpiece of your fall foliage itinerary.
The roughly 70-minute round-trip ride follows the Lehigh River through the gorge, winding past towering cliffs, tunnels, and dense forests that turn brilliant shades of red, orange, and gold.

You get all the drama of a mountain foliage excursion without having to hike to the top of a mountain. For the best panoramic views, secure a ticket for the railway’s Vista Dome cars for a sky-high perspective of the gorge.
Get the postcard view from above

For the classic “Little Switzerland of America” view, head to Flagstaff Mountain Overlook, where you can look down over Jim Thorpe’s historic rooftops and the surrounding mountains. The entire town appears tucked into the valley below, making it pretty easy to understand where the nickname comes from.
To get closer to the leaves, cross the Mansion House Pedestrian Bridge into Lehigh Gorge State Park for an easy walk or bike ride along the river beneath the towering, forested slopes.

Shutterstock / EQRoy
Where to eat, drink, and stay
After a day of leaf-peeping, settle into Jim Thorpe’s cozy downtown.

For dinner, Marion Hose Bar is a local favorite housed in a historic firehouse, with a menu of American comfort food and cocktails that fits the town’s old-world atmosphere. For something casual and lively, grab a drink and a bite at Moya, known for its Latin-inspired menu.

If you want to lean all the way into Jim Thorpe’s historic charm, spend the night at the Inn at Jim Thorpe, a Victorian-era hotel right in the heart of downtown that puts you within walking distance of Broadway. For an even more atmospheric stay, The Harry Packer Mansion offers overnight accommodations inside one of the town’s most recognizable historic homes.

Jim Thorpe’s downtown is compact enough to wander on foot, and once the sun goes down, the Victorian buildings, mountain backdrop, and twinkling storefronts make the whole place feel especially magical in fall.

Source / Pocono Mountains
Fall events worth planning around
For the ultimate autumn visit, you’ll want to plan your trip around the 2026 Jim Thorpe Fall Foliage Festival.
Taking place across the first three weekends in October (Oct 3-4, 10-11, and 17-18), the festival transforms the town into a full blown autumn celebration.

Colorful leaves drift across cobblestone streets, craft and food vendors line the sidewalks, and local storytellers share haunted legends by lantern light. The festival features four separate live music locations, giving the entire town an incredible, lively energy.
There’s truly nothing like it!
What to know before you go
Where: Jim Thorpe, PA, in Carbon County, nestled in the foothills of the Pocono Mountains along the Lehigh River

From NYC: Jim Thorpe is roughly 100 miles northwest of Midtown Manhattan. Driving generally takes around two hours, depending on traffic, via I-80 West. (While you can take a bus to nearby Lehighton, having a car makes exploring the overlooks and state parks much easier)
Best time for foliage: Mid- to late October. Exact timing changes every year, so check the foliage tracker immediately before booking an overnight stay
